Best Travel Backpacks For Kids

By Marcus Webb · April 5, 2026 · Updated August 30, 2026

Most kids’ backpacks look similar in a product photo and behave very differently after three months of actual use. We focused this review on the details that show up after real wear — zipper durability, strap adjustability, and whether it survives a spilled drink — rather than just capacity and looks.

What we looked for

A good kids' travel backpack needs to survive more than one trip — it becomes the school bag, the weekend bag, and the travel bag within about a month. We prioritized durable zippers, a chest strap that actually stays fastened, and enough structure that it doesn't collapse into a shapeless sack half-full.

Other options worth considering

Character-branded options from major toy retailers

A reasonable budget pick for younger kids specifically motivated by a favorite character, though zipper quality is noticeably lower than the dedicated travel brands on this list.

Hardshell mini backpacks

More protective for electronics or a tablet, but heavier and less comfortable for a full day of wear than a soft-sided option.

What held up and what didn't

Across a school year plus four trips, the main failure point on cheaper backpacks was the zipper pulls, which several kids managed to break off within a few months. The backpacks that held up best had oversized, kid-manageable zipper pulls and a bar-tacked stress point at the top of each zipper.

Pros and cons

What we liked

  • Chest strap keeps the bag from sliding off shoulders on a long walk through an airport
  • Front pocket sized for a passport wallet and a small stuffed animal — surprisingly important to kids
  • Wipeable material handles the inevitable spilled juice box

Worth knowing

  • Smaller capacity than some parents expect from photos — check liters, not just the picture
  • Some straps aren't adjustable enough for kids who'll use the bag for more than 1–2 years

Frequently asked questions

What size backpack does a kid need for air travel?

A 10–14 liter bag is usually enough as a personal item for a child, holding a tablet, a small toy, snacks, and a change of clothes.

Should a kid's travel backpack have wheels?

For kids under about 6, a wheeled option can be easier through long airport walks; older kids generally do fine with a standard backpack and a chest strap.

How do you stop a kid's backpack zipper from breaking?

Look for oversized, easy-to-grip zipper pulls and reinforced stitching at the top of each zipper — this is the most common failure point on lower-quality kids' backpacks.
